title: The Blaschka Object Network — Dealer Archive Register
scope: Archival survival of the three documented commercial dealer/distributor routes for Blaschka marine-invertebrate models: Henry Augustus Ward / Ward's Natural Science Establishment, Robert Damon / Robert Ferris Damon, and Václav Frič / V. Frič. The register separates workshop-side business evidence, dealer-side corporate survival, customer-side correspondence, museum acquisition files, and later business-context records.
methodological_guard: A museum holding objects bought from a dealer is not a dealer archive unless a named correspondence, acquisition, accounts, catalogue, invoice, or business-record series can be identified. Dealer correspondence is not treated as Blaschka-specific until the document, finding aid, or an archival reconstruction explicitly establishes that link. 'No dedicated corporate fonds identified' records the result of this public-catalogue pass only and is not proof that records do not survive.

status_vocabulary.intact_business_archive: A named personal and/or corporate archive survives as a collection of record.
status_vocabulary.distributed_business_correspondence: No dedicated corporate fonds has been identified; the business must be reconstructed across workshop, customer, museum, and manuscript repositories.
status_vocabulary.direct_blaschka_dealer_evidence: The source explicitly concerns Blaschka models, catalogue, order, payment, agency, packing, shipment, receipt, breakage, or resale.
status_vocabulary.receiving_side_dealer_file: A customer or museum record explicitly documents transactions with the dealer but Blaschka content must be checked item by item.
status_vocabulary.general_dealer_business_context: Same-period business correspondence documenting the dealer's commercial practice without establishing a Blaschka transaction.
status_vocabulary.post_production_business_context: Dealer-business material after the marine-model production period; useful for institutional continuity and commercial practice only.

signatures.dealer: Henry Augustus Ward / Ward's Museum, Rochester
signatures.title: Erwerbungen bei Ward's Museum of Mineralogy, Geology & Zoology (Rochester)

cross_dealer_comparators.research_value: The same receiving institution and administrative series preserves dealer-specific acquisition files for all three major Blaschka distribution routes. Even if individual files contain no glass models, they offer an unusually controlled comparison of nineteenth-century natural-history dealership, ordering, pricing, documentation, and museum receipt practices.
cross_dealer_comparators.blaschka_guard: The finding aid establishes dealer-specific acquisition files, not Blaschka content. Each file requires inspection before any Blaschka transaction is asserted.

dealers.name: Henry Augustus Ward / Ward's Natural Science Establishment
dealers.blaschka_market: North America, with wider international museum trade

core_archive.repository: Rare Books, Special Collections, and Preservation, University of Rochester
core_archive.institutional_status: University of Rochester identifies Henry Augustus Ward as a collection of record and preserves both personal/family papers and the corporate archive of Ward's Natural Science Establishment.

direct_blaschka_transaction_witnesses.repository: Academy of Natural Sciences of Drexel University Archives
direct_blaschka_transaction_witnesses.source: Ward's Museum of Mineralogy, Geology and Zoology pamphlet
direct_blaschka_transaction_witnesses.evidence: The archival item is catalogued under Leopold and Rudolf Blaschka and the related Blaschka collection finding aid identifies the pamphlet as advertising Ward's sale of Blaschka glass models.

direct_blaschka_transaction_witnesses.repository: Boston Society of Natural History / successor archive context
direct_blaschka_transaction_witnesses.evidence: Project primary-source reconstruction records a Ward-mediated second invoice and delivery to the Boston Society of Natural History in summer 1880. The Blaschka commission and the dealer invoice are kept as distinct transaction layers.

direct_blaschka_transaction_witnesses.repository: Auckland War Memorial Museum manuscript collections
direct_blaschka_transaction_witnesses.evidence: Cheeseman–Ward correspondence documents a Blaschka catalogue request, exchange terms, sample request, seven supplied models, payment routing, and an unrealised larger order. Ward appears as catalogue distributor, supplier, exchange broker, and credit/payment intermediary.

direct_blaschka_transaction_witnesses.repository: University of Rochester, Henry Augustus Ward Papers
direct_blaschka_transaction_witnesses.evidence: Project reconstruction identifies Ward's offer to the Columbian Museum and the subsequent purchase contract for the broader World's Columbian Exposition collection, which included Blaschka marine models. The $95,000 figure belongs to the broader collection purchase and is not a Blaschka subset price.

receiving_side_and_distributed_witnesses.collection: SIA RU000189, Assistant Secretary in charge of the United States National Museum Records
receiving_side_and_distributed_witnesses.evidence: Henry Augustus Ward correspondence; the finding aid says the bulk concerns business transactions between the U.S. National Museum and Ward's Natural Science Establishment, especially taxidermic work and exchange of natural-history specimens.
receiving_side_and_distributed_witnesses.blaschka_guard: Blaschka content has not been isolated at item level.

receiving_side_and_distributed_witnesses.collection: SIA RU000208, National Museum of Natural History Division of Mammals Records
receiving_side_and_distributed_witnesses.evidence: A long Ward's Natural Science Establishment correspondence file overlaps the late Blaschka marine-model period.
receiving_side_and_distributed_witnesses.blaschka_guard: No glass-model content is asserted without inspection.

receiving_side_and_distributed_witnesses.repository: Alexander Turnbull Library / National Library of New Zealand
receiving_side_and_distributed_witnesses.evidence: Ward letters to Julius von Haast survive together with a microfilm sequence of Haast letters to Ward, creating a two-direction dealer/customer corpus.
receiving_side_and_distributed_witnesses.blaschka_guard: The collection is a major same-period Ward route but individual letters require Blaschka-specific checking.

receiving_side_and_distributed_witnesses.repository: Cornell University Library, Division of Rare and Manuscript Collections
receiving_side_and_distributed_witnesses.collection: John Henry and Anna Botsford Comstock papers
receiving_side_and_distributed_witnesses.evidence: Three Henry Augustus Ward letters survive in a Cornell scientific correspondence archive during the active Blaschka trade.
receiving_side_and_distributed_witnesses.blaschka_guard: Content has not been verified as glass-model business.

receiving_side_and_distributed_witnesses.evidence: Dealer-specific acquisition file for Ward's Museum of Mineralogy, Geology & Zoology, Rochester.
receiving_side_and_distributed_witnesses.blaschka_guard: No Blaschka content asserted without file inspection.

later_business_context.repository: American Museum of Natural History, Gottesman Research Library
later_business_context.collection: Henry Augustus Ward papers relating to the Ward-Coonley collection of meteorites

later_business_context.repository: American Museum of Natural History, Gottesman Research Library
later_business_context.evidence: Later Ward's Natural Science Establishment correspondence includes specimen negotiations, postal receipts, estimates, account statements, invoices, and shipping-insurance certificates, making it useful for the firm's mature documentary practices.

critical_gaps: The Rochester archive is clearly the central dealer corpus, but a public item-level list of Blaschka-specific order books, invoices, customer correspondence, and shipping records has not been recovered in this pass.
The next gain is document retrieval inside A.W23 and D.231, not further discovery of generic Ward references.
Customer-side Ward files must be cross-walked against workshop account/order dates before individual letters are promoted to Blaschka evidence.

dealers.name: Robert Damon / Robert Ferris Damon
dealers.blaschka_market: Great Britain and Ireland, with additional international natural-history trade

workshop_side_core.repository: Juliette K. and Leonard S. Rakow Research Library, Corning Museum of Glass
series: Drafts of business letters, 1880–1885, Box 13 / Microfiche 15,211
direct_blaschka_cluster: September 1880 draft establishing Damon as the principal/sole agency route for Great Britain and Ireland in the relevant correspondence context
10 February 1883 draft concerning Henry Woodward and a British Museum catalogue/order enquiry
28 October 1883 draft referring to British Museum and Marlborough College orders
November 1883 request for additional packing money
28 November 1883 dispatch/account material and Lieferungs-Buch model list
workshop_side_core.research_value: Agency rules, prepayment, mark-up freedom, order aggregation, prices, packing, insurance, breakage, institutional customers, and routing decisions.

direct_blaschka_transaction_witnesses.node: British Museum / Natural History Museum London
direct_blaschka_transaction_witnesses.evidence: Published archival reconstruction based on Rakow business drafts and delivery records links Damon to the British Museum order, packing charges, insurance, dispatch, and breakage complaint. The publication is a guide to the primary archive rather than a substitute for the original documents.

direct_blaschka_transaction_witnesses.node: Jeypore Museum / Albert Hall Museum, Jaipur
direct_blaschka_transaction_witnesses.evidence: Project workshop OCR records Damon arranging or advancing payment for an amended Jeypore Museum order. The models were stated at 640 Marks before the full packing/freight account; two large cases were expected and the full total was expected above 700 Marks. Later correspondence asks Damon about routing; final dispatch used packages LB 285–286 by rail to Trieste, Austro-Hungarian Lloyd to Bombay, with approximately 698 Marks prepaid and an approximately 61.5-Mark balance.
direct_blaschka_transaction_witnesses.guard: OCR quality is uneven; figures are preserved as documentary layers and no corrupt apparent total is converted into an object count.

direct_blaschka_transaction_witnesses.node: Liverpool Museum / Free Public Museum of Liverpool
direct_blaschka_transaction_witnesses.evidence: Workshop correspondence places the Liverpool commission in the Damon agency sequence. Project reconstruction separates a 247-Mark models-only figure, an approximately 50-Mark packing estimate, a later dispatch-letter invoice OCR of 268 Marks, and freight case mark I.B. 268 routed through M. O. W. Möller in Hamburg.
direct_blaschka_transaction_witnesses.guard: The father/son identity behind every 'Mr Damon' letter is not assigned without image-level verification; the 21-Mark arithmetic difference is not labelled as a historical charge.

receiving_side_and_distributed_witnesses.evidence: The Robert Damon authority record identifies ten letters created by Damon and one letter to Damon. Creator dates are 25 October 1877; 26 April 1878; 15 January, 13 February, 3 March, and 9 April 1879; and 5 January, 22 February, 21 March, and 21 April 1881. The recipient-side letter is dated 7 February 1881.
verified_item_examples: CA MUA MG1022-2-1-117-0019 — Robert Damon to John William Dawson, 25 October 1877
CA MUA MG1022-2-1-135-0011 — Robert Damon to John William Dawson, 13 February 1879
CA MUA MG1022-2-1-136-0004 — Robert Damon to John William Dawson, 3 March 1879
receiving_side_and_distributed_witnesses.correction_guard: CA MUA MG1022-2-1-109-0007, dated 13 February 1877, is a C. A. White letter and must not be cited as Damon.
receiving_side_and_distributed_witnesses.blaschka_guard: Searchable catalogue metadata does not expose the letter texts sufficiently to claim Blaschka content.

receiving_side_and_distributed_witnesses.collection: Zoology and Palaeontology departmental correspondence and acquisition records
receiving_side_and_distributed_witnesses.evidence: The NHM Damon authority record exposes a long purchasing and correspondence relationship with Robert Damon across zoology and palaeontology.
receiving_side_and_distributed_witnesses.blaschka_guard: Only records independently tied to Blaschka orders should be promoted to direct Blaschka evidence.

receiving_side_and_distributed_witnesses.evidence: Dealer-specific acquisition file for Robert Damon of Weymouth.
receiving_side_and_distributed_witnesses.blaschka_guard: No Blaschka content asserted without inspection.

receiving_side_and_distributed_witnesses.collection: John Ruskin letters to Robert Damon
receiving_side_and_distributed_witnesses.evidence: Thirteen autograph letters concern minerals and Ruskin's dealings with Damon, providing same-period evidence of Damon's customer practice outside Blaschka trade.

receiving_side_and_distributed_witnesses.repository: Museum of New Zealand Te Papa Tongarewa Archives
receiving_side_and_distributed_witnesses.evidence: Robert Damon letter concerning dispersal of the Godfrey Collection.

critical_gaps: No dedicated Damon firm archive, invoice series, order book, or incoming-correspondence fonds surfaced in this broad public-catalogue sweep.
The workshop's outgoing business drafts are much more visible than the dealer's incoming side, producing a structural asymmetry in the surviving archive.
The McGill 10+1 sequence is now bibliographically controlled, but its item texts still need direct inspection for catalogues, prices, glass models, remittances, or order references.
NHM Damon files need item-level inspection against the Rakow dates to distinguish general specimen trade from Blaschka agency business.

dealers.name: Václav Frič / V. Frič natural-history and teaching-aids business
dealers.blaschka_market: Austria-Hungary with additional international resale routes
dealers.business_history_guard: The firm continued under Jaromír Frič after Václav and ended in 1959. The National Museum in Prague received remaining natural-history stock. Transfer of stock is not proof that the company's complete paper archive was transferred.

workshop_side_core.repository: Juliette K. and Leonard S. Rakow Research Library, Corning Museum of Glass
workshop_side_core.series: Blaschka business notebooks, accounts, and letter drafts
workshop_side_core.direct_blaschka_anchor: 8 November 1884 draft to Václav Frič concerning a commercial shipment and four glass models sent as a gift to the Prague museum.
workshop_side_core.research_value: Reseller relations, shipment composition, gifts, catalogue commerce, and workshop-side dealer correspondence.

direct_blaschka_transaction_witnesses.records: Trustee Minutes, Outward Letter Books, purchase-of-specimens correspondence, and historical registers
direct_blaschka_transaction_witnesses.evidence: The museum's archival reconstruction identifies the instruction to Frič to obtain Blaschka glass invertebrates and later correspondence concerning three mixed consignments. Project backend preserves the route as Blaschka workshop → Frič → Australian Museum.

direct_blaschka_transaction_witnesses.records: Museum accession/registry records, read against Rakow workshop correspondence
direct_blaschka_transaction_witnesses.evidence: The 8 November 1884 workshop draft is joined to a museum accession record for four Blaschka models delivered through Frič; project reconstruction keeps model catalogue numbers 36, 224, 235, and 553 distinct from museum accession numbers.

direct_blaschka_transaction_witnesses.repository: Stift Kremsmünster / Sternwarte natural-history collection records
direct_blaschka_transaction_witnesses.evidence: Published and project provenance reconstruction gives the chain Blaschka workshop → Václav Frič → Karl Eggerth senior → Stift Kremsmünster. Exact Frič invoice, quantity, price, and object list remain open.

receiving_side_and_distributed_witnesses.evidence: The museum's official archive description explicitly lists correspondence with Václav Frič's natural-history trade in Prague. The same written-records collection includes correspondence, catalogues, object lists, administrative files, and collection documentation.
receiving_side_and_distributed_witnesses.access_constraint: The written records collection is inaccessible from 1 July 2026 and is expected to remain inaccessible until the fourth quarter of 2027; enquiries can still be directed to the archive.

receiving_side_and_distributed_witnesses.title: Zoologie: Erwerbungen von der Lehrmittel- und Naturalienhandlung V. Fric in Prag
receiving_side_and_distributed_witnesses.blaschka_guard: Dealer-specific acquisition file; Blaschka content unknown until inspection.

receiving_side_and_distributed_witnesses.title: Erwerbungen beim Naturalienhändler V. Fric (Prag)
receiving_side_and_distributed_witnesses.blaschka_guard: The file is a dealer-specific acquisition record, not direct proof of Blaschka content.

receiving_side_and_distributed_witnesses.repository: Archivo del Museo Nacional de Ciencias Naturales, CSIC, Madrid
receiving_side_and_distributed_witnesses.collection: Personal Científico Ignacio Bolívar y Urrutia — Correspondencia. Entidades
receiving_side_and_distributed_witnesses.evidence: Digitised original letter from Václav Frič in Prague to Ignacio Bolívar offering insects for purchase; the catalogue explicitly identifies V. Fric. Lehrmittel und Naturalien-Handlung.
receiving_side_and_distributed_witnesses.blaschka_guard: This is same-period dealer-business evidence, not a Blaschka transaction.

receiving_side_and_distributed_witnesses.collection: Antonín Frič personal fonds and National Museum institutional records
receiving_side_and_distributed_witnesses.evidence: The archive preserves Antonín Frič's written estate and institutional museum records relevant to the museum-side dealer network.
receiving_side_and_distributed_witnesses.identity_guard: Antonín Frič's personal fonds is distinct from the commercial papers of Václav Frič's firm; the two must not be conflated.

later_business_context.evidence: Three items from V. Frič, Prague; useful for later commercial continuity only unless content establishes an earlier collection link.

later_business_context.repository: Grigore Antipa National Museum of Natural History, Bucharest
later_business_context.evidence: Published archival research reports five Václav Frič letters to Grigore Antipa, together with labels and historical inventory/register evidence. This is a useful dealer/customer corpus but falls after the marine-model production period.
later_business_context.source_guard: The five-letter count is retained as a published archival report; a current public item-level finding aid has not been recovered in this pass.

critical_gaps: No dedicated V. Frič company correspondence/account archive surfaced in this public-catalogue sweep.
The relationship between company stock transferred to the National Museum in 1959 and surviving business papers remains unresolved.
The newly identified Museum für Naturkunde Berlin correspondence is a major lead, but physical access to the written-records collection is currently suspended until the expected Q4 2027 reopening.
Hildesheim and BayHStA dealer-specific files should be inspected before they are connected to Blaschka models.
Dealer-side order books, invoices, customer ledgers, and shipment accounts remain the decisive missing source for reconstructing Frič's Blaschka network at scale.

negative_search_audit.Damon: No dedicated Damon corporate fonds or business order-book series was identified in the broad public archive-catalogue sweep. Evidence remains distributed across Rakow, McGill, NHM, BayHStA, Morgan, Te Papa, and transaction-specific institutional archives.
negative_search_audit.Fric: No dedicated V. Frič corporate fonds was identified. Strong business correspondence survives in Museum für Naturkunde Berlin and several receiving-side dealer files; later company-stock transfer to the National Museum is not treated as archival transfer proof.
negative_search_audit.Ward: No archival absence problem comparable to Damon or Frič: Rochester is clearly the collection of record. The remaining problem is item-level targeting inside a large surviving personal/corporate corpus.

closure_statement: The broad dealer-archive discovery phase is frozen at this version. Further additions should be evidence-led: a newly identified named record group or item, a digitised document, a published archival citation with usable reference, or an archivist/curator response. Research effort should now move from discovering repositories to retrieving and cross-walking documents across workshop → dealer → customer → museum accession chains.
network_observation: The archival asymmetry is historically productive. Ward survives as a concentrated personal/corporate archive; Damon and Frič survive as distributed business archives reconstructed from the Blaschka workshop and receiving institutions. The same commercial network therefore produces different archival topologies, and provenance has to be rebuilt across institutional boundaries rather than assumed to reside in one dealer fonds.
